Click STIG Viewer Version 3.x-Win64_msi. 3. Click Save to save as U_STIGViewer-win32_x64-3-x-x_msi.zip. 4. Open the downloaded ZIP file. Open the enclosed .msi file to begin the installation process. Administrative rights are required for installation. |
| Verifying integrity of packages | A file containing secure hash values for the STIG Viewer ZIP packages is published on cyber.mil. Hash values are provided for SHA256, SHA384, and SHA512. To verify, compute the hash value on the STIG Viewer package under inspection using Get-FileHash cmdlet (Windows PowerShell) or sha256sum, sha384sum, and sha512sum programs (Linux). Compare the published hash value to the computed value for the same algorithm. |
| Unblocking on Windows | STIG Viewer downloaded on Windows may be marked as downloaded from the internet and may prevent running the application. This can also apply to ZIP contents when extracted. Consult the local system administrator for guidance. If approved, unblock via File Explorer > Properties > General tab > Security section > check Unblock > OK. Alternatively, use the Unblock-File cmdlet in Windows PowerShell. |
| Linux File Access Policy | Linux systems using fapolicyd may block execution and present “Operation Not Permitted” or “cannot open shared object file” when launching STIG Viewer. Procedure: 1. sudo mkdir /opt/stigviewer 2. sudo unzip U_STIGViewer-linux_x64-3-x-x.zip -d /opt 3. sudo mv /opt/stig_viewer_3-linux-x64 /opt/stigviewer 4. sudo fapolicyd-cli --file add /opt/stigviewer 5. sudo fapolicyd-cli --update 6. Run STIG Viewer from /opt/stigviewer/STIG\ Viewer\ 3 |
| Digital signatures | Beginning with STIG Viewer version 2.15, Windows EXE and MSI files are digitally signed with a DOD code signing certificate. Information on installing DOD trust anchors is available at https://public.cyber.mil/pki-pke/. To view signatures, open file properties in Windows Explorer and select the Digital Signatures tab. |
| STIG Viewer Help | The STIG Viewer Help section can be found under the hamburger menu. It provides links to the Release Notes, Dependency List, User Guide, and Check for Updates, which is a link to Cyber Exchange to verify the latest version available. |
| Opening STIG Viewer | Windows standalone package: start by opening the STIG Viewer 3.exe file. Windows MSI package: start by opening the STIG Viewer 3 item from the Start Menu. Linux standalone package: start the standalone STIG Viewer executable from the command line (STIG Viewer 3). Other considerations: consult local system administrators for assistance in running standalone versions with application firewalls. At startup, the application opens to the Home page. |
| Theme setting | To change appearance from Default to Dark mode: select hamburger menu > Preferences > under Theme, change to Dark > click Save. |

### STIG Explorer / STIG handling

| Area | Extracted details |
|---|---|
| Open STIGs | Open STIGs from the Home screen or by selecting the STIG Viewer icon on the left side of the screen. |
| Open STIGs from Home Screen | 1. Click Open in the upper portion of the STIG Viewer section of the screen. 2. Navigate to the location of the STIG and double-click or select the STIG and then click Load. Note: user can import either .ZIP/.zip or .XML/.xml formats. |
| Open STIGs from STIG Viewer Icon | 1. Click the STIG Viewer icon on the Home page. 2. Click the Open STIG icon in the upper portion of the screen. |
| Main sections after opening STIG | SECTION 1: STIG Overview shows the STIG’s associated documents, such as Read Me, Release Memo, Overview, Revision History, etc. User can show or hide these documents via checkbox in the Gear icon. Read Me, Release Memo, Overview, and Revision History files appear only if the ZIP file has been opened. SECTION 2: Rules shows the Group ID. User can add Rule ID and/or STIG ID, or any combination of the three, by selecting the gear icon in the navigation bar. Default is Group ID for the Origin STIG. User can also choose to show or hide the Rule Title via checkbox. SECTION 3: Vulnerability detail shows more details about each vulnerability in the selected STIG or more detailed information about a selected rule/requirement. |
| Adding STIGs to the Library | 1. Click the STIG Viewer icon on the Home page or the magnifying glass icon in the upper-right portion of screen. 2. Click the Add STIG to Library icon in the upper portion of the screen. Note: if no STIGs are loaded into the library, message displays: “Your STIG library is empty! Visit public.cyber.mil to download: Individual STIGs or A Collection of all STIGs Then use: Open STIG or Add STIG to Library to view or add them to your collection”. Links go to the public version of Cyber Exchange. 3. Download the desired STIGs. 4. Click Add STIG to Library and navigate to the location of the STIGs to be imported. Note: user can select .ZIP/.zip or .XML/.xml file formats. 5. Select the file(s) and click Load. Note: user can import the Compilation file to load all the STIGs. A counter displays the import progress. 6. Once loaded, the screen updates. |
| Viewing multiple STIGs | 1. Click Open Multiple STIGs in upper-right portion of screen. 2. Checkboxes appear beside STIGs in the Library to select STIGs to view. Note: Select All selects all listed STIGs. Clear Selected unselects all checked STIGs. If more than one version of a STIG exists, an expansion arrow appears beside the STIG name; once expanded, the user can select one or multiple versions of the STIG to add to the view. 3. Search for STIGs that contain a common word by entering the search word in the search field located in the list of STIGs. 4. Once selected, click Filter icon or Open X STIGs, where X represents the number selected. |
| View Multiple STIGs – Filtered | Requirements can be filtered on Content, Title, Severity, STIG ID, Group ID, Rule ID, CCI ID, and Legacy ID. Filter options can be any combination of: contains; does not contain; is; is not; is greater than; is less than. Note: not all options available for each category; Severity provides three choices in the drop-down menu. Open X STIGs opens selected STIGs. Funnel icon at top left indicates number of filters applied and can be clicked to view the filter. Filter carried over from STIG selection to view; further filters can be added via funnel icon at top of left column. Gear icon changes left-column display: default Rule List Display shows Group ID; user can add Rule ID and/or STIG ID and change header order by unselecting all and clicking in desired order; Group By can be changed from Origin STIG to None; Rule Title can be removed by unchecking Show Rule Title. Sort ascending/descending by clicking selected ID headers. Create a checklist by selecting Create checklist from filtered rules. Export STIGs to HTML and CSV by selecting Export STIGs and choosing format and fields. Fields are divided into Header and Rule Info. All fields export unless deselected by clicking the file name to unhighlight it. After all fields selected, click Export and choose export location. |
| View Multiple STIGs – Unfiltered | Select Add STIG to Library and navigate to STIG location. Select STIGs to bring into STIG Viewer. User can also bring in the entire Compilation file and choose STIGs from the list. Click Open Multiple STIGs in top-right corner and select checkbox beside STIGs to bring in together. Click Open X STIG, where X represents the number selected. Each STIG is listed on the left pane, with respective documents first. To view all requirements together, select gear icon to change view and select None. If None selected and Show Rule Title unchecked, requirements are listed in Group ID in ascending or descending order. Add a filter to narrow down requirements; requirements that do not meet filter are listed below filtered requirements. Create a checklist of filtered requirements by clicking gear icon and selecting Create checklist from filtered rules. Export STIGs to HTML and CSV by selecting format and fields to export. All fields export unless deselected by clicking field name; fields divided into Header and Rule Info. For filtered items, Filtered Rules selections are made in the Export Type area. After fields selected, click Export and choose export location. |
| Viewing more STIGs | View another STIG or combined STIGs by selecting the + tab in the upper portion of the screen. This opens the STIG Viewer explorer main page where user can add more STIGs or open STIGs already in the list. The Recent STIGs section shows a list of recently opened STIGs. To open a recently opened STIG, click the STIG. If a STIG was opened and not saved to the library, it is displayed in Open Results; to view a STIG, click the STIG name in the Open Results section. |
| Remove STIGs | To remove a STIG not loaded in the Library, click the X to the right of the STIG name. To remove STIGs loaded in the Library, click Delete STIGs and then check the box beside the STIGs to be removed and click Delete X STIGs, where X represents the number selected. Users can Select All STIGs or Clear Selected STIGs. |
| Keyword Search | Search all STIGs listed in the user’s library that contain a certain word by entering the word in the search box at the top of the screen. A list of all Rules containing the search word appears. Click Open All in Explorer to open the STIG Explorer details screen showing all STIGs containing the search term in the main section and all individual Rules in the left pane. Scroll through listed STIGs and click a STIG to view all Rules for that STIG that contain the search term. Click a Rule in the main pane to view Rule details. |
| Comparing STIGs | The user can compare differences between two versions of a STIG. Note: load STIGs in correct order; older STIG must be loaded into the Library first, followed by newer STIG. 1. Ensure both versions are listed in the STIG Library and click Compare STIGs in upper-right portion of screen. 2. Select the older version for the Right and the newer version for the Left, then click the Compare STIGs button at the bottom of the page. Note: Benchmark Dates should be used to determine older/newer version because when a major release occurs, release number resets back to “1.” 3. Users can scroll through rules and look for Changed rules (orange-colored asterisk), Added rules (green-colored plus sign), and Removed rules (red-colored X), or apply a Diff Status filter to view only Unchanged, Changed, Added, or Removed by clicking the funnel icon. |

### Checklist structure, fields, statuses, import/export

| Area | Extracted details |
|---|---|
| Create Checklist from Home Page or Top Navigation Bar | If STIGs are loaded into the library, checklists can be created by clicking the checklist icon (three lines and a checkmark at the top of the screen) or clicking the Checklists section at the bottom of the Home page. Click Create Checklist to create a new checklist or Load Checklist to open an existing V3 checklist. Checklists created in STIG Viewer 2.x can be imported by clicking the hamburger menu and selecting Import V2 Checklist. Users can import multiple STIG Viewer 2.x checklists into STIG Viewer 3.x by navigating to a central location and selecting the desired checklists. After clicking Create Checklist, a prompt to name the checklist appears; after entering a name, click Create Checklist. User selects STIGs from the left pane; if no STIGs are loaded in the library, use the STIG Explorer button to add STIGs. If STIGs are loaded, select STIGs by clicking the + beside the STIG name. Search field can be used to find STIGs. Clicking + beside STIG name adds all rules to the main pane for inclusion in the checklist. To select individual rules, click the magnifying glass beside the STIG name and click + beside desired rules; selected rules are listed in the far-right pane. Back to Checklist Builder returns to STIG selection pane. Fill Checklist begins processing. Users can add classification to user-controlled pieces of the checklist (Comments, Finding Details, and Target Data) by opting in Preferences: Always Show Classification Options and then click Edit Classification Levels. Higher classification levels in the list take priority; if a document has both CUI and FOUO items, CUI is displayed on the banner. STIG details display combined severities and individual tabs for each severity. Target Data is on the right portion of the screen along with a graph of Rule Statuses and respective counts. Score updates as rule status updates, using rule status and weight to determine checklist score. Rule List Display can add Rule ID and STIG ID to the left pane and Group By can change from Origin STIG to None. Edit Checklist allows adding/removing STIGs. Remove a STIG by clicking the trash can icon beside the STIG name in the main pane. Add a STIG by clicking the + beside the name in the left pane. Save finishes creating the checklist. Saved checklist appears on homepage under Checklists section. |
| Create Another Checklist | To add a checklist from the STIG Checklists page, click the Add (+) tab, select Create Checklist, enter a name, then click Create Checklist. |
| Opening an Existing Checklist | Open by navigating to Home page and selecting one of the checklists listed or clicking Open and navigating to the checklist location. Another option is to click the Checklists icon on the left. Select one of the Recent Checklists or click Load Checklist and navigate to the checklist to be loaded. If a checklist is already open, click the Add (+) tab to open a new screen. |
| Changing status of rules | Mark requirements as Open, Not A Finding, Not Reviewed, or Not Applicable by clicking the circle beside the Rule. Click once to set status to Not a Finding (green checkmark), twice to Open (red exclamation mark), three times to Not Applicable (black circle with slash), four times to Not Reviewed (gray blank circle). To update multiple rules, select rules using SHIFT or CTRL, then click the desired status at the top of the center pane. Score updates as statuses change. Circle beside the ID reflects assigned status. |
| Override Severity Status | Users can override a severity status by clicking on the severity and then changing the severity to a different value. User must select the new severity, which triggers the requirement of an Override Reason. Users must provide an override reason for the severity to change. Click Save to save the severity change. An asterisk appears beside the Severity showing that it has been overridden. |
| Filtering a Checklist | Filter rules by clicking the funnel icon and applying filters. The number of filters applied is shown beside the funnel icon. Rules matching the filter are listed. Change from Group ID to Rule ID or STIG ID in the left column by selecting the gear icon. |
| Populating Target Data | Target data can be populated on the far-right side of the screen. This area also displays a graphic showing the number of rules in the STIGs included in the checklist, the progress of status changes, and the Score. If target data has a classification already set, or if “Always Show Classification Options” is enabled in preferences, the classification level of the target data can be set using the classification editor button at the top of the target data section. Hovering over the graphic displays a download symbol to obtain a copy of the graphic for presentations. |
| Adding Comments and Finding Details to a Single Rule | Add Comments and Finding Details to an individual rule by typing directly into the Comments and Finding Details boxes or copying and pasting from another document into the boxes. |
| Adding Comments and Finding Details to Multiple Rules | Multiple rules can be updated at one time. After selecting rules, click the square in the upper-right portion of the screen. From the pop-up menu, select Edit Comments or Edit Finding Details. After selection, either type or copy and paste in the box. Click Save to add the text to the selected rules. All Rules selected will have the same Comment or Finding Details text. |
| Saving a Checklist | An unsaved checklist has an asterisk beside the checklist name. In Preferences, the default is Auto-Save Checklists; uncheck to save manually. To save, click Save in the upper part of the screen or click the hamburger menu. The hamburger menu provides Save, Save As, or Save All open checklists (only shows if more than one checklist is open and unsaved), which prompts the user to save each open checklist separately. Navigate to the desired location and save each open checklist. If exiting a checklist not updated, application closes with no prompts. If updates were made, user is prompted to Close without Saving, Save and Close, or Cancel; Cancel is default. After saving, checklist can be reopened by clicking name in Recent Checklists or by Load Checklist and navigating to saved location. |
| Importing XCCDF Results into a Checklist | Click Import icon and select Import XCCDF or CMRS Results. Navigate to results file and click Load. Pop-up shows: number of results with matching Rule IDs and revision numbers ready to import; number of results with matching Rule IDs but not matching revision number; any results that did not match a Rule ID; Incoming checklist has target data. This wording only shows if checklist contains target data. Complete import with only matching revision numbers by clicking Complete Import. To bring in all results regardless of revision matches, check Include loosely matched results then click Complete Import. If any rules did not match, click Show to display unmatched rules. If file contains target data, pop-up allows include or exclude target data and view the target data being imported. Imported results show in checklist. |
| Importing Checklist Data | Click Import and then select Import Checklist Data. This brings in Status, Comments, Finding Details, and Target Data from the checklist being imported. Navigate to checklist file and click Load. Pop-up shows: number of results with matching Rule IDs and revision numbers ready to import; number of results having matching Rule IDs but that did NOT match on revision number; note to include loosely matched results via checkbox; this wording shows only if the checklist contains Rule IDs that did not match on revision number; any results that did NOT match a Rule ID; this wording shows only if the checklist contains Rule IDs that did not match on Rule ID; if some incoming Rules have Comments or Finding Details, user can select what to do with those Comments and Finding Details. Options are: Replace existing. Append to existing. Ignore incoming. Incoming checklist has target data; this wording shows only if checklist contains target data. |
| Exporting Checklist Data | Click Export icon to export checklist data. Pop-up window shows export format and fields to include. Defaults are HTML format and All fields. Possible formats are HTML, CSV, CMRS XML, CKL (SV v2 format), and CKLB. CKLB format can now be imported into eMASS. Users can exclude fields from each section by clicking the caret to display fields for each section and clicking None to exclude all the fields or clicking a field to exclude it. Any fields not highlighted will be excluded from export. |
| Resizing the Checklist Pane | To resize vertically, click the bar between the rule list and the rule details and drag left or right. To resize horizontally, click the bar between the rule details and the Comments and Finding Details and drag up or down. |

### Applicability Guide / asset collection structure

| Area | Extracted details |
|---|---|
| Accessing Applicability Guide | To access existing Applicability Guides, select the Open icon and navigate to the existing location. To create a new collection, select the New icon or click the Applicability Guide icon. |
| Menu | Hamburger menu is in the upper-left corner. It is divided into FILE, APP, and HELP. It also contains Exit. |
| File Menu | FILE section allows the user to create a new asset collection or open an existing one. |
| App Menu | Preferences menu allows the user to set preferences such as enable sunset labels, change the font size, access application logs, change the theme, set the Default App for which application to open when accessing STIG Viewer, and reset the application back to default settings. |
| Navigation Bar Menu | Navigation bar displays options to interact with the application and the created collection. When viewing a collection, buttons appear such as Save, Merge, etc. Merge button opens a file dialog and select a collection file to merge into the open collection. Save button opens a file dialog, name the collection file, and save it to disk. Export button expands into four options. |
| Right-Click Menu | Right clicking an asset provides shortcuts to add an asset, edit the asset, remove the asset, and enter Guide Mode. It also includes Add Parent and Add Parent using Guide Mode. These two features are only available if the selected asset and its current parent have matching assets. |
| Asset Tree overview | The main view under the File menu is the Asset Tree. It allows the user to view their current collection and add, edit, or remove assets. Based on selections, a pane to the right can appear to display or collect additional information about the selection. The asset the user is working with will be highlighted in green. |
| Creating a Collection | Click the Applicability Guide icon on the home page or click the icon in the navigation bar at the top. Enter a name for the collection, and then click Create. Note: to go straight to a collection without naming it, click New in the Applicability Guide section of the home page. |
| Adding Assets (Standard Mode) | 1. Click the “+” button to add the first Asset. 2. A selection pane appears to the right, and the selected asset is highlighted in green. Enter the Asset Name and select the Asset Type that applies to this asset. 3. After the Asset Type is selected, applicable labels for the asset can be selected. Select zero or more labels that apply to the asset, and then click Create to create entries in the asset tree representing that item. Use the search input to find desired labels quickly. Note: user can replace No Name by using Edit Asset. Asset Label is defined as “A descriptive tag that applies to an asset type.” |
| Adding Assets (Guide Mode) | 1. Click the compass icon (circle with a diamond) next to the “+” button to begin Guide Mode. 2. After clicking Guide Mode, a pane appears to the right prompting the user to add an asset by asking a series of questions. Answer Yes or No to each appropriate question and select End Guide when finished. 3. Select No to move to the next asset in the list. Select Yes to move to the label pane where name and the asset type label can be selected (if available). 4. After adding and creating an asset, the wizard descends into its children; the next prompt will be the first child of the asset just added. After a decision is made to add each child, the wizard returns to the top level, and other assets can be added. Notes: Select multiple labels to create multiple tree items with the different labels selected. To leave Guide Mode, click End Guide. |
| Adding Parent Assets | After an asset has been created, a new parent can be added by using the Add Parent feature. Note: Add Parent is only available if an asset type is available that allows relationships between the selected asset and its current parent. 1. Right-click the asset and select Add Parent. 2. Select the asset to add and click Create. Note: listed on the right are assets available based on the asset selected and its current parent. 3. The new parent will be added to the asset. |
| Adding Parent Assets (Guide Mode) | If an asset has been created but reverse order is desired, a parent can be added using Guide Mode by clicking the Add Parent option when selecting Guide Mode. Note: Add Parent is only available if an asset type is available that allows relationships between the selected asset and its current parent. 1. Right-click the asset and select Guide Mode >> Add Parent. 2. On the right, select Guide Mode to view available asset labels based on the asset selected and its current parent. 3. Select Yes on the Asset Type, name it, select the label to add, and then click Create. 4. The new parent will be added to the asset. 5. Click End Guide. |
| Editing Assets | 1. After creating an asset, click the pencil icon to begin editing an asset. A pane appears on the right side with the current asset information. 2. Change the name of the asset and the label if available and click Save. 3. The changes will be reflected on the tree to the left. |
| Removing Assets | To remove an asset, click X next to the tree item and click Delete. |
| Save, Open, and Merge overview | When an asset posture is built, the application allows the user to save the collection as a JSON document for import later. These options can be found under the File menu located under the hamburger menu or by using the Save icon at the top of the page. |
| Save Collection | 1. To save a collection, select the Save icon in the navigation bar or open the hamburger menu and select File >> Save. 2. A window pops up with the option to choose a save location and a file name if this is a new collection. Click Save to save the collection. |
| Open Collection | 1. To open an Asset Collection (either JSON or XML), click Load Collection to load an existing collection or select from the Recent Collections section of the main page. Note: alternatively, click the hamburger menu and select File >> Open. 2. Navigate to the saved Asset Collection document, select it, and click Load. Note: if an imported asset has been sunset or deprecated, an indicator is displayed next to the asset. A red sun indicator signifies that it is sunset. To view the names of sunset assets, select File >> Preferences and check Enable Sunset Labels. |
| Merge Collection | Merging an asset collection allows the user to import assets from an asset collection file into the currently open collection. When successful, the assets of the merged collection are appended to the end of the current collection. 6.5.4.1 Merge an Asset Collection: 1. In the Navbar, click the Merge icon. 2. Navigate to the saved Asset Collection document, select it, and click Load. |
| Drag and Drop | The SRG/STIG Applicability Guide is drag-and-drop enabled; the user can drag and drop a compatible asset into another asset. To drag and drop an asset, left-click and hold with the left mouse button and then drag it to the intended asset. When the dragged asset encounters a compatible asset, the compatible asset turns green, signaling a valid drop location. If incompatible, the asset is not moved and a message is displayed. |
| Exports overview | After building an asset collection, the user can export the requirements/policy documents using options in the Navbar menu. Exports come in two file types, HTML and text, and in two varieties, normal/flat and asset-based list. The flat list contains only the policy documents and their information; the asset-based list also contains the asset that it applies to and the path to get to that asset. |
| Preview | To access a preview of the current collection, select Documents from the asset tree. The window on the right shows a list of the Requirements/Policy Documents that apply to the current asset posture. |
| Exporting | 1. To export assets, select Export Assets as Text (or as HTML) in the Navbar. 2. In the pop-up menu, choose the location and name of the export file and click Save. |
| Scenario | A task is required to secure a system on a VMware-based cloud environment. The VM is running Windows 11 and has several applications installed, including JRE 8, Microsoft Office 2016, and .Net Framework 4.0. Securing this system requires knowing what policy documents to follow. Therefore, the SRG/STIG Applicability Guide is used to fill this need easily and quickly. Then steps are given to add a cloud service asset, a VM, Windows 11 operating system, and the applications JRE 8, Microsoft Office 2016, and .Net Framework 4.0 using Guide Mode. |

### Fields, headings, values explicitly stated

| Item | Extracted fields / values |
|---|---|
| Export STIG fields | Fields are divided into two sections: Header and Rule Info. All fields are exported unless the user deselects them by clicking the file name to unhighlight it. |
| Checklist export fields | Users can exclude fields from each section by clicking the caret to display fields for each section and clicking None to exclude all the fields or clicking a field to exclude it. Any fields not highlighted will be excluded from the export. |
| STIG viewer rule display fields | Group ID; Rule ID; STIG ID; Rule Title; Origin STIG; None |
| Filterable rule fields | Content; Title; Severity; STIG ID; Group ID; Rule ID; CCI ID; Legacy ID |
| Search restrictions | Searches may also be restricted to Content (Discussion, Check, and Fix), Rule Title, Severity, STIG ID, Group ID, Rule ID, CCI, or Legacy ID. |
| Checklist statuses | Open; Not A Finding; Not Reviewed; Not Applicable |
| Severity override | Override Reason required |
| Checklist import retained data | Status; Comments; Finding Details; Target Data |
| Checklist export formats | HTML; CSV; CMRS XML; CKL (SV v2 format); CKLB |
| Asset collection file formats | JSON; XML |
| Asset export file types | HTML; text |
| Asset export varieties | normal/flat; asset-based list |
| Asset selection fields | Asset Name; Asset Type; applicable labels; Asset Label |
| Classification-related fields/options | Always Show Classification Options; Edit Classification Levels; classification level of target data; banner color; higher classification levels take priority; CUI; FOUO; Unknown |
| Theme options | Default; Dark |
| Help links | Release Notes; Dependency List; User Guide; Check for Updates |
| Integrity algorithms | SHA256; SHA384; SHA512 |

### Frequencies, cadences, SLAs, escalation, exceptions, roles

| Requested category | Extracted details |
|---|---|
| Cadence/frequency | No recurring cadence, schedule, SLA, severity thresholds, escalation path, exception workflow, RACI, or operational ownership is explicitly stated in the page. |
| Roles/responsibilities | The page mentions “local system administrator” and “consult local system administrators” for guidance with Windows unblocking and application firewalls. No other roles or responsibilities are defined. |
| Audit evidence / artifacts | Exported STIG data can be saved as HTML and CSV. Checklist data can be exported as HTML, CSV, CMRS XML, CKL (SV v2 format), and CKLB. CKLB can be imported into eMASS. The checklist graphic can be downloaded for use in presentations. STIG packages include Read Me, Release Memo, Overview, Revision History. The Applicability Guide can export requirements/policy documents as HTML or text, in flat or asset-based list. Open Results and Recent STIGs / Recent Checklists / Recent Collections are listed views, but no audit evidence workflow is described. |
| POA&M / remediation records | No POA&M, remediation record, exception, waiver, or formal defect-tracking template is explicitly described in the page. The only related fields are rule status, severity override, comments, finding details, target data, and imported automated review results. |
| Task/ticket/playbook templates | No task ticket, playbook, or SOP template headings are explicitly provided. The closest structured templates are checklist export field sections “Header” and “Rule Info,” and asset export varieties “normal/flat” and “asset-based list.” |
| Escalation/exception handling | No escalation or exception-handling process is explicitly stated beyond prompts for save/close/cancel on unsaved checklists and use of local system administrator for unblocking/application firewall guidance. |
| SLA/severity values | No SLA values are stated. Severity-related behavior stated only: user can override severity to a different value; Severity provides three choices in the drop-down menu when filtering; severity override requires an Override Reason; an asterisk indicates overridden severity. |

title: Program Manager's Handbook JSIG-RMF
content:
### Handbook structure relevant to operational runbook/SOP, recurring execution, evidence, POA&M/remediation, roles, templates, escalation, cadence, and fields captured | Section / Phase | Explicitly stated operational content | |---|---| | **1.1 Purpose and Scope** | - High-level process overview
- Relationship between SDLC and RMF
- Roles and responsibilities
- Information on the steps in the RMF process
- Key deliverables | | **1.3 Handbook Maintenance** | - The DoD Joint SAP Cybersecurity (JSCS) Working Group (WG) will review and evaluate this PM Handbook annually and update as appropriate. | | **3 RMF PROCESS** | - Six (6) Steps of the RMF are described
- Security authorization artifacts used by the Authorizing Official (AO) to make an informed risk-based decision whether to grant an ATO | | **RMF Step 1—Categorize Information System (IS)** | - Purpose: Categorize an IS by first categorizing the information on the system according to the potential impact of a loss of Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability (C-I-A)
- SDLC Phase: Initiation | | **RMF Step 2—Select Security Controls** | - Purpose: Select security controls using appropriate baseline and overlay(s), then tailor as required to prevent security breaches of an IS
- SDLC Phase: Initiation | | **RMF Step 3—Implement Security Controls** | - Purpose: Security controls are implemented on the information system
- SDLC Phase: Development/Acquisition, Implementation | | **RMF Step 4—Assess Security Controls** | - Purpose: Determine the extent to which the security controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome in meeting security requirements
- SDLC Phase: Development/Acquisition; Implementation | | **RMF Step 5—Authorize Information System** | - Purpose: Identify weaknesses or deficiencies to be corrected and any residual vulnerabilities and submit a security authorization package to the AO (via the SCA) for adjudication
- SDLC Phase: Implementation | | **RMF Step 6—Monitor Security Controls** | - Purpose: Assess and track the security state of an information system and its operational environment
- SDLC Phase: Operational/Maintenance/Disposal | ### Roles and responsibilities | Role | Explicit responsibilities / statements | |---|---| | **Agency/Element Head (Government)** | - Ultimate responsibility for mission accomplishment and execution of business functions
- Responsible for adequately mitigating risks to the element, its individuals, and the Nation
- Defines priorities to ensure collaboration and information-sharing sufficient to ensure both element and DoD SAP Community-wide mission accomplishment
- Responsible for ensuring that: (i) information security management processes are integrated with strategic and operational planning processes; (ii) senior officials within the organization provide information security for the information and information systems that support the operations and assets under their control; and (iii) the organization has trained personnel sufficient to assist in complying with information security requirements in related legislation, policies, directives, instructions, standards, and guidelines | | **Risk Executive (Function) Government** | - May be fulfilled by an individual, a group, or an assigned function within an organization
- Directly supports the AO
- Ensures risk-related considerations for individual information systems, to include authorization decisions, are viewed from an organization-wide perspective
- Ensures managing information-system-related security risks is consistent across the organization, reflects organizational risk tolerance, and is considered along with other types of risks in order to ensure mission/business success | | **Chief Information Officer (CIO) (Government)** | - Along with the Element Head and other senior officials, ensures that information systems are acquired and information resources are managed in a manner consistent with laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, regulations, as well as priorities established by the Element Head
- Develops, maintains, and ensures the implementation of sound, secure, integrated, IS architectures
- Promotes the effective, efficient design, development, and operations of all major information and resource management processes | | **Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)/Senior Information Security Officer (SISO)** | - Executes the CIO’s responsibilities under the Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA) of 2002
- Serves as the CIO’s liaison to the DoD SAP organization’s AOs, ISO, Common Control Providers (CCP), and ISSO/ISSM | | **Authorizing Official (AO) (Government)** | - Senior official or executive with authority to formally assume responsibility for operating an IS at an acceptable level of risk to organizational operations, organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and national security
- May have budgetary oversight for an IS or be responsible for the mission/business operations supported by the system
- Accountable for security risks associated with information system operations
- May appoint one or more Delegated Authorizing Officials (DAO) in writing to expedite authorizations of designated systems and provide mission support
- Determines the acceptable level of risk associated with a given information system and the collective risk to the organization from information systems operating across the organization
- Takes under advisement observations and concerns from members of the REf including the Director of Security, CIO, CISO, et.al, when making an acceptable risk determination | | **Delegated Authorizing Official (DAO) (Government)** | - Delegated authority by an AO to carry out specific activities for specific systems as identified by the AO (e.g., authorizations to operate) | | **Security Control Assessor (SCA)** | - Appointed in writing by the AO to act on his or her behalf to conduct a security assessment
- Responsible for conducting a comprehensive assessment of the management, operational, and technical security controls employed within or inherited by an IS
- Determines overall effectiveness of the controls
- Provides an assessment of the severity of weaknesses or deficiencies discovered in the IS and its environment of operation
- Recommends corrective actions to address identified vulnerabilities
- Loyalty is to the AO
- Will inform the PM/ISO whether an assessment is satisfactory or not and whether the system is being maintained at an acceptable level of risk | | **Common Control Provider (CCP)** | - Responsible for the development, implementation, assessment, and monitoring of common controls
- Organizations can have multiple CCPs depending upon how information security responsibilities are allocated organization-wide | | **Information Owner/Steward (Government)** | - Organization official with statutory, management, or operational authority for specific information
- Responsible for establishing the policies and procedures governing generation, collection, processing, dissemination, and disposal of information | | **Mission/Business Owner (MBO) (Government)** | - Has operational responsibility for the mission or business process supported by the mission/business segment or the information system
- Key participant/stakeholder regarding system life-cycle decisions | | **Information System Owner (ISO)** | - Responsible for overall procurement, development, integration, modification, operation, maintenance, and disposal of an information system (and system components)
- Responsible for development and provision of the SSP and every other document required for security ATO
- Responsible for ensuring that the program ISSM and ISSE are identified
- Focal point for the IS
- ISSM and ISSE support the ISO and serve as a central point of contact regarding the authorization process
- PM/ISO responsibilities are also described as including all ISO tasks in the RMF | | **Information System Security Engineer (ISSE)/Information Assurance Systems Architect and Engineer (IASAE)** | - Ensures that information-security requirements are effectively implemented throughout the security architecting, design, development, configuration, and implementation processes
- Coordinates security-related activities with ISOs, ISSOs/ISSMs, and CCPs | | **Information System Security Manager (ISSM)/Information System Security Officer (ISSO)** | - Appointed in writing by the ISO
- Responsible for maintaining the day-to-day security posture and continuous monitoring of a system
- Responsible for the overall IA of a program, organization, system, or enclave | | **PM/ISO delegation statement** | - PM/ISO frequently delegates document development (e.g. SSP, SCTM, RAR, ConMon Plan, Security Assessment Plans, et.al.) to the ISSM/ISSO (or ISSE if the system has one)
- Responsibility for ensuring the documents are completed, accurately reflecting the system and environment, and in a timely manner to allow for assessment and authorization to operate to meet mission needs remains with the PM/ISO | ### Process, cadence, and recurring execution requirements | Item | Explicitly stated cadence / recurring requirement | |---|---| | **Handbook review** | Annually by the JSCS WG | | **Continuous monitoring model** | Continuous monitoring of security controls and periodic reauthorization | | **RMF Step 6 compliance** | Each Program must “test” at least one-third of the security controls annually and verify the continued compliance of the remaining controls | | **Three-year authorization period** | By the end of the three-year authorization period, every control will have been tested at least once | | **Assessment frequency guidance** | Critical or more volatile controls should be assessed more frequently, e.g. quarterly, semi-annually; more static controls may be assessed once every three years | | **ConMon reporting** | Continuous monitoring compliance will be reported at least annually to the respective AO | | **ConMon report submission** | A ConMon Report is submitted to the AO/SCA at least annually | | **Document updates in Step 6** | All documents created earlier, as well as the system inventory, are updated as needed (at least annually) as part configuration management and monitoring activities | ### Security authorization artifacts / evidence / body of evidence | Artifact | Explicitly stated contents / purpose / usage | |---|---| | **Security Authorization Package** | - Includes security authorization artifacts submitted for AO adjudication
- PM/ISO will sign off on the Security Authorization Package before forwarding it to the SCA/AO, indicating the documentation accurately reflects the configuration and security state of the IS and environment in which it operates | | **Body of Evidence (BoE)** | - Security authorization artifacts submitted as part of the Security Authorization Package | | **System Security Plan (SSP)/Security Controls Traceability Matrix (SCTM)** | - Provides an overview of security requirements, description of agreed-upon controls and other supporting security-related information | | **Risk Assessment Report (RAR)** | - Defines the organizationally established level of acceptable risk associated with operation of an IT system at a specific level; identifies risks; provides an assessed residual-risk-level for the system | | **Continuous Monitoring (ConMon) Plan** | - Provides the strategy to routinely evaluate selected IA controls/metrics | | **Security Assessment Report (SAR)** | - Contains security control assessment results and recommended corrective actions for security-control weaknesses and deficiencies | | **Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M)** | - Defines plans of action and milestones related to correcting weaknesses or deficiencies, reducing or eliminating known vulnerabilities, and identifies completion dates | | **Security Assessment Plan** | - Provides a roadmap for how the assessment will be conducted, the type of assessment
- May also be updated during the process to include assessment procedures and an explanation of how the assessment results were achieved
- Also referred to as the Security Assessment Plan and Procedures | | **Authorization Decision Document** | - Conveys the final security authorization decision (i.e., ATO, DATO, IATT) from the authorizing official, any terms and conditions for authorization, and the authorization termination date if appropriate
- If the authorization decision document is classified, a memo may be provided in lieu of the decision document | | **Documented evidence of correction** | - Examples stated: scan results, registry “dumps,” etc. | | **Updated system inventory** | - Deliverable for decommissioning strategy execution | ### POA&M / remediation / corrective action handling | Item | Explicitly stated handling details | |---|---| | **Task 5-1—Prepare the POA&M** | - Based on the findings and recommendations of the SAR, excluding any remediation actions taken
- SCA documents initial findings
- ISO completes POA&M; adds additional items; includes CCP, if finding is against a common control | | **PM/ISO responsibilities for POA&M** | - Responsible for completing the POA&M fields, updating, and resolving POA&M items | | **Task 4-4—Initial remedial actions** | - Conduct initial remedial actions on security controls based on the findings and recommendations of the SAR and reassess remediated control(s), as appropriate | | **Task 6-3—Remediation actions** | - Conduct remediation actions based on the results of ongoing monitoring activities, assessment of risk, and outstanding items in the POA&M | | **Task 6-4—Update artifacts based on monitoring** | - Update the SSP, SAR, and POA&M based on the results of the continuous monitoring process | | **Security Assessment Report content** | - Issues, findings, recommendations from the security control assessment | | **POA&M content** | - Weaknesses or deficiencies
- Plans of action and milestones related to correcting weaknesses or deficiencies
- Reducing or eliminating known vulnerabilities
- Completion dates | ### Security control selection / tailoring / overlays / documentation fields | Item | Explicitly stated details | |---|---| | **Step 2 task 2-1** | - Identify the security controls provided by the organization as common controls for organizational IS and document the controls in the SSP | | **Step 2 task 2-2** | - Select the security controls for the IS (baseline, overlays, tailored) and document the controls in the SSP | | **Step 2 task 2-3** | - Develop a strategy for the continuous monitoring of security control effectiveness and any proposed or actual changes to the IS and its environment of operation | | **Step 2 task 2-4** | - Review and approve the draft SSP by the AO or DAO | | **SCTM fields/details explicitly stated** | - Lists all controls selected for the system
- Additional details on each control, e.g. implementation status, monitoring frequency, etc. | | **Task 2-2 four-step process** | - Step 1: Select the initial baseline set of security controls specifying type: common, system-specific, or hybrid
- Step 2: Select and apply security control overlays
- Step 3: Tailor (in or out) the set of security controls
- Step 4: Supplement the tailored set of security controls | | **Tailoring documentation requirement** | - Tailoring decisions, including the specific rationale (i.e., mapping to risk tolerance), are documented in the SSP for the information system | | **Unimplemented selected control** | - If a selected control is not implemented, the rationale for not implementing the control must be documented in the SSP | | **Overlay conflict handling** | - If use of multiple overlays results in conflicts between application or removal of security controls, the AO (or designee), in coordination with the information owner/steward, will resolve the conflict | | **Overlay change documentation** | - If a control is added or removed by application of an overlay, the SSP should reflect the change with the justification being the application of the specific overlay(s) directing the change | | **Final security controls** | - The final set of tailored and/or supplemented security controls must be submitted for approval to the respective AO prior to finalizing implementation | ### Tables and named frequencies / values preserved | Table / named item | Explicitly stated fields / values | |---|---| | **Table 2: RMF Step 1 - Categorize IS** | - Task 1-1—Categorize the Information System and document the results in the SSP → Primary Responsibility: ISO or Information Owner/Steward → Deliverable(s): Draft SSP with System Categorization filled in
- Task 1-2—Describe the information system (including system boundary) and document the description in the SSP → Primary Responsibility: ISO → Deliverable(s): Updated SSP to include a description of the IS
- Task 1-3—Register the IS with the appropriate organizational program management offices → Primary Responsibility: ISO → Deliverable(s): Document or entry in the IT registry with the official system name, system owner, and categorization | | **Table 3: Confidentiality Impact Level** | - Classification TS//SAR or S//SAR → Confidentiality Impact Level: Moderate
- Adjustment to Impact Level: Adjust to the High Confidentiality Impact Level if any user lacks either the required security clearance or the required citizenship (address with overlay) | | **Table 4: System Integrity and Availability Categorization Example** | - Information Type A: Integrity L, Availability L
- Information Type B: Integrity H, Availability M
- Information Type C: Integrity M, Availability M
- Overall System Categorization per Objective: Integrity H, Availability M | | **Table 5: RMF Step 2 - Select Security Controls** | - Task 2-1—Identify common controls → Primary Responsibility: CCP; ISO, ISSM/ISSO, ISSE, SCA → Deliverable(s): Document the common controls in the SSP/SCTM
- Task 2-2—Select the security controls for the IS (baseline, overlays, tailored) → Primary Responsibility: ISO; ISSE → Deliverable(s): Document the selected security controls in the SSP/SCTM, Draft RAR
- Task 2-3—Develop strategy for continuous monitoring → Primary Responsibility: ISO or CCP → Deliverable(s): Documented and approved Continuous Monitoring (ConMon) Plan/Strategy including frequency of monitoring for each control
- Task 2-4—Review and approve the draft SSP → Primary Responsibility: AO or DAO; ISSM/ISSO → Deliverable(s): Documented and approved Draft SSP/SCTM | | **Table 6: Security Control Baseline Examples** | - Control IDs and titles shown include AC-1 Access Control Policy And Procedures; AC-2 Account Management; AC-2(1) Account Management; AC-2(2) Account Management; AC-2(3) Account Management; AC-2(4) Account Management; AC-2(5) Account Management; AC-2(6) Account Management; AC-2(7) Account Management; AC-2(8) Account Management; AC-2(9) Account Management; AC-2(10) Account Management; AC-2(11) Account Management; AC-2(12) Account Management; AC-2(13) Account Management; AC-3 Access Enforcement; AC-3(1) Access Enforcement; AC-3(2) Access Enforcement; AC-3(3) Access Enforcement; AC-3(4) Access Enforcement
- Symbols used: X, blank, -, +
- In JSIG October 9, 2013, each ‘X’ was replaced with ‘C’, ‘H’, or ‘S’ to provide tentative designation for enforcement/responsibility | | **Table 7: RMF Step 3 - Implement Security Controls** | - Task 3-1—Implement the security controls specified in the SSP → Primary Responsibility: ISO or CCP
- Task 3-2—Document the security control implementation, as appropriate in the SSP, providing a functional description of the control implementation → Primary Responsibility: ISO or CCP; ISSM/ISSO; ISSE → Deliverable(s): Updated SSP with information describing how security controls are implemented | | **Table 8: RMF Step 4 - Assess Security Controls** | - Task 4-1—Develop, review, and approve a plan to assess the security controls → Primary Responsibility: ISSM/ISSO; ISSE; SCA → Deliverable(s): Security Assessment Plan
- Task 4-2—Assess the security controls in accordance with the assessment procedures defined in the Security Assessment Plan → Primary Responsibility: SCA → Deliverable(s): Individual test results for each test or matrix for all tests
- Task 4-3—Prepare the SAR documenting the issues, findings, and recommendations from the security control assessment → Primary Responsibility: SCA → Deliverable(s): Security Assessment Report (SAR)
- Task 4-4—Conduct initial remedial actions on security controls based on the findings and recommendations of the SAR and reassess remediated control(s), as appropriate → Primary Responsibility: ISO or CCP; SCA; ISSM/ISSO → Deliverable(s): Updated Risk Assessment Report (RAR) | | **Table 9: RMF Step 5 - Authorize Information System** | - Task 5-1—Prepare the POA&M based on the findings and recommendations of the SAR, excluding any remediation actions taken → Primary Responsibility: SCA (document initial findings); ISO (completes POA&M; adds additional items; includes CCP, if finding is against a common control) → Deliverable(s): POA&M
- Task 5-2—Assemble the Security Authorization Package to include artifacts and submit the package to the AO for adjudication → Primary Responsibility: ISO; ISSM/ISSO; SCA → Deliverable(s): Security Authorization Package; artifacts include: SSP/SCTM, SAR, POA&M, RAR, and ConMon Plan
- Task 5-3—Determine the risk to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, or reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, or the Nation → Primary Responsibility: AO or DAO
- Task 5-4—Determine if risk to organizational operations, organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, or the Nation is acceptable → Primary Responsibility: AO → Deliverable(s): Authorization decision document (e.g. ATO, DATO, IATT) | | **Step 5 DATO handling** | - If a Security Authorization Package is submitted with a request for ATO and the package is incomplete or unsatisfactory, the AO will not normally issue a DATO; the AO will more likely send the package back to the PM/ISO with instructions on why it was returned
- DATO is most frequently issued when a system was granted an ATO and the conditions under which the ATO was granted have deteriorated
- DATO may also be issued if the PM/ISO did not ensure the Security Authorization Package was submitted in a timely manner to allow the AO/SCA to review the package
- If submitted in a timely manner but AO/SCA not able to review before ATO expires, the AO will likely extend the existing ATO, e.g., for three (3) months, either via memo or verbally
- Send a follow-up email to the AO reiterating the extension for records or request a memo | | **Table 10: RMF Step 6 - Monitor Security Controls** | - Task 6-1—Determine the security impact of proposed or actual changes to the IS and its environment of operation → Primary Responsibility: ISO or CCP; ISSO/ISSM → Deliverable(s): Change Request
- Task 6-2—Assess a selected subset of security controls employed within and inherited by the IS in accordance with the organization-defined monitoring strategy → Primary Responsibility: SCA; ISSO/ISSM → Deliverable(s): Periodic Continuous Monitoring Report
- Task 6-3—Conduct remediation actions based on the results of ongoing monitoring activities, assessment of risk, and outstanding items in the POA&M → Primary Responsibility: ISO or CCP; ISSM/ISSO → Deliverable(s): Documented evidence of correction such as scan results, registry “dumps,” etc.
- Task 6-4—Update the SSP, SAR, and POA&M based on the results of the continuous monitoring process → Primary Responsibility: ISO or CCP → Deliverable(s): SSP, SAR, RAR, and POA&M
- Task 6-5—Report the security status of the IS (including effectiveness of security controls employed within and inherited by the IS) to the AO and other appropriate organizational officials on an ongoing basis, in accordance with the Monitoring Strategy → Primary Responsibility: ISO or CCP → Deliverable(s): Periodic Continuous Monitoring Report
- Task 6-6—Review the reported security status of the IS on an ongoing basis in accordance with the monitoring strategy to determine whether the risk remains acceptable → Primary Responsibility: AO → Deliverable(s): ATO
- Task 6-7—Implement an IS Decommissioning Strategy, when needed, which executes required actions when a system is removed from service → Primary Responsibility: ISO → Deliverable(s): Updated system inventory | ### Explicit absence statements in the page - No explicit RACI matrix labeled as such is provided. - No explicit ticket template is provided. - No explicit playbook template headings are provided. - No explicit exception request form is provided. - No explicit escalation workflow table is provided beyond the stated AO/DAO/SCA return, approval, extension, and conflict-resolution actions.

title: SAP RMF Checklist
content:
- **Document title:** SAP RMF Checklist
- **Version:** 1.1
- **Document type:** Special Access Program (SAP) Risk Management Framework (RMF) Cybersecurity Compliance Checklist
- **Fields at top of page:**
  - Reviewer: [__________]
  - Date: [__________]
  - Organization: [__________]
  - System: [__________]

- **Scope / use statements:**
  - This checklist does not replace the AO/DAO-approved SSP or SCTM for a particular system.
  - Evidence of system specific continuous monitoring results for a system can be provided to satisfy these self-assessment requirements if the scope of continuous monitoring assessments includes the items on this checklist.
  - This checklist serves as an aid for the inspection and assessment of information systems, networks, and components under the purview of the Department of Defense (DoD) Special Access Program Central Office (SAPCO) and DoD Service/Agency SAPCOs.
  - Based on the criteria specified within the JSIG, this checklist may be used in conjunction with the SAP Security Compliance Checklist in preparation for formal inspections and staff assistance visits.

- **Instructions / exception handling fields:**
  - Check Yes or No based on self-assessment of the organization and/or system(s) implementation.
  - Enter "S" for SCTM into the Yes column if deviations from the JSIG requirements exist that are approved in the SCTM.
  - Enter "P" for POA&M in the No column if deviations are documented in a POA&M that has been accepted by the AO.
  - For Non-Tailorable controls if "No" then indicate in the remarks if the Senior AO for the system has endorsed a waiver.

- **Checklist response columns:**
  - ID#
  - Questions
  - References
  - Yes
  - No
  - N/A
  - Remarks

- **Section headings and checklist items with cadence, roles, artifacts, approvals, and fields captured:**

| Section | ID# | Question / Requirement | References | Cadence / SLA / Threshold | Roles / Approvals / Artifacts / Fields |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES | 1 | Are the ISSM, and/or ISSO appointed to their position and performing their responsibilities as per the JSIG? | JSIG 1.5.14; JSIG 1.5.15 |  | ISSM; ISSO |
| ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES | 2 | Are privileged users adhering to, and performing their duties, as per their established role-based responsibilities, acceptable system use agreement, privileged user guides, etc.? | JSIG 1.5.16; JSIG PL-4; JSIG PS-6 |  | privileged users |
| POLICY AND PROCEDURES | 3 | Have tailored controls been reviewed at least annually as part of the continuous monitoring program? | JSIG Chapter 3, Page 3-43 | at least annually | continuous monitoring program |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 4 | Are procedures in place for (a)creating, (b)activating, (c)modifying, (d)monitoring, (e)disabling, and (f)removing accounts that comply with provisions outlined in the JSIG? | JSIG AC-2 |  | procedures; accounts |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 5 | Are accounts reviewed at least annually for changes in personnel status? | JSIG AC-2 | at least annually | accounts; personnel status |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 6 | Are all accounts which have been inactive for a minimum of 90 days automatically disabled? | JSIG AC-2(3) | minimum of 90 days | accounts |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 7 | If the site has unattended processing requirements, are the procedures: (1) Documented? (2) Approved by the AO/DAO? (3) Implemented as approved? | JSIG SSP 3.1; JSIG AC-11; JSIG AC-3 |  | AO/DAO approval; documented procedures |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 8 | If the site has periods processing requirements are the procedures: (1) Documented? (2) Approved by the AO/DAO? (3) Implemented as approved? | JSIG SSP 4.0; JSIG SC-4; JSIG SC-4(2); JSIG AC-3 |  | AO/DAO approval; documented procedures |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 9 | Are procedures for all manual Data Transfers between IS, also known as Assured File Transfers (AFT): (1) Documented? (2) Approved by the AO/DAO? (3) Implemented as approved? | JSIG AC-4; JSIG AC-3 |  | AO/DAO approval; documented procedures |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 10 | Are duties of individuals with SAP IS access separated to prevent malicious activity without collusion? (At a minimum, system administrators shall not also perform security audit functions, and DTAs shall not perform media custodian duties without explicit AO/DAO approval.) | JSIG AC-5 |  | system administrators; security audit functions; DTAs; media custodian duties; explicit AO/DAO approval |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 11 | Is the principle of least privilege implemented and enforced, allowing only authorized accesses for users that are necessary to accomplish assigned tasks, and is assignment of privileged use reviewed on a quarterly basis? | JSIG AC-6; JSIG AC-6(7) | quarterly | privileged use |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 12 | Are privileged users (except the DTA role) required to use separate, non-privileged accounts when performing non-privileged functions? | JSIG AC-6(2) |  | privileged users; DTA role |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 13 | Are the number of super user (administrator/root) accounts strictly limited to the maximum extent possible? | JSIG AC-6(5) |  | super user accounts |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 14 | Are user accounts locked after a maximum of 3 unsuccessful logon attempts within a 15 minute time period requiring an administrator to unlock the account? | JSIG AC-7 | maximum of 3 unsuccessful logon attempts within a 15 minute time period | administrator unlock |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 15 | Do all IS display the current DoD Notice and Consent Banner, retain the message until the user acknowledges the usage conditions, and take explicit actions to log on to, or further access, the information system? | JSIG AC-8 |  | current DoD Notice and Consent Banner; user acknowledgment |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 16 | Do all SAP IS implement a screen lock within 15 minutes of user inactivity or upon initiation by the user? | JSIG AC-11 | within 15 minutes of user inactivity | screen lock |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 17 | Is a password required for reentry into the system following the session being locked? | JSIG AC-11 |  | password |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 18 | When activated, does the session lock place an unclassified pattern onto the display? | JSIG AC-11(1) |  | unclassified pattern |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 19 | Are usage restrictions/requirements documented for wireless access? | JSIG AC-18 |  | documented restrictions/requirements |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 20 | If allowed, are all wireless access methods documented and approved by the AO? | JSIG AC-18 |  | documented; AO approval |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 21 | Does the organization monitor for unauthorized wireless access points/connections? | JSIG SI-4 |  | monitor unauthorized wireless access points/connections |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 22 | Are usage restrictions/requirements documented for mobile devices? | JSIG AC-19 |  | documented restrictions/requirements |
| ACCESS CONTROL | 23 | If allowed, are mobile devices documented and approved by the AO? | JSIG AC-19 |  | documented; AO approval |
| AWARENESS AND TRAINING | 24 | Is Privileged User training provided to users assigned to positions requiring privileged access before authorizing access to SAP IS, prior to performing assigned duties, when required by system changes, and at least annually thereafter? | JSIG AT-3; JSIG PL-4 | before authorizing access; prior to performing assigned duties; when required by system changes; at least annually thereafter | Privileged User training; users assigned to positions requiring privileged access |
| AWARENESS AND TRAINING | 25 | Are all personnel performing privileged user functions (e.g., security audits, system/network administration, database administration, DTA, etc.) current on training and certification(s) applicable for the position they hold? | DoD 8570.1-M or replacement; JSIG AT-3; JSIG AT-4 |  | personnel performing privileged user functions |
| AUDIT AND ACCOUNTABILITY | 26 | If automated audit collection is not supported, is use of manual audits documented in the SSP and approved by the AO? | JSIG AU-1 |  | manual audits; SSP; AO approval |
| AUDIT AND ACCOUNTABILITY | 27 | Are all SAP IS configured to audit the events specified in AU-2 of the JSIG? | JSIG AU-2 |  | audit events |
| AUDIT AND ACCOUNTABILITY | 28 | Are all SAP IS configured to capture the following content, at a minimum, for each audited event: (1)User ID (2)Type of event/action (3)Success or failure of event/action (4)Date (5)Time (6)Terminal or workstation ID (7)Entity that initiated event/action (8)Entity that completed event/action (9)Remote Access | JSIG AU-3 |  | User ID; Type of event/action; Success or failure of event/action; Date; Time; Terminal or workstation ID; Entity that initiated event/action; Entity that completed event/action; Remote Access |
| AUDIT AND ACCOUNTABILITY | 29 | Is auditing configured and audit record storage capacity allocated to reduce the likelihood of such capacity being exceeded? | JSIG AU-4 |  | audit record storage capacity |
| AUDIT AND ACCOUNTABILITY | 30(1) | Are the audit logs/reports (manual and automated) reviewed at least weekly, or at a frequency approved in the SSP? | JSIG AU-6 | at least weekly, or at a frequency approved in the SSP | audit logs/reports (manual and automated); SSP approval |
| AUDIT AND ACCOUNTABILITY | 30(2) | Are the results of these reviews documented in either an electronic or manual log? | JSIG AU-6 |  | electronic or manual log |
| AUDIT AND ACCOUNTABILITY | 31 | Does the IS use an internal system clock for audit time stamps, and are all clocks accurate to within one minute? | JSIG AU-8 | within one minute | internal system clock |
| AUDIT AND ACCOUNTABILITY | 32 | Does the SAP IS protect audit information and audit tools from unauthorized access, modification and deletion? | JSIG AU-9 |  | audit information; audit tools |
| AUDIT AND ACCOUNTABILITY | 33 | Does the organization limit access to audit functionality to only a small subset of privileged users? | JSIG AU-9(4) |  | privileged users |
| AUDIT AND ACCOUNTABILITY | 34 | Are audit records retained for a minimum of five (5) years for SAP information? (The AO has the authority to scale back the retention period depending on the mission of the IS. Such relief must be documented in writing). | JSIG AU-11 | minimum of five (5) years | AO; documented in writing; retention relief |
| SECURITY ASSESSMENT AND AUTHORIZATION | 35 | Are all connections of an IS to an external IS documented in the SSP and authorized through an ISA, if applicable? | JSIG CA-3 |  | SSP; ISA |
| SECURITY ASSESSMENT AND AUTHORIZATION | 36 | Have all IS POA&Ms been updated at least quarterly by the ISO and/or delegate (e.g., ISSM/ISSO)? | JSIG CA-5 | at least quarterly | ISO; delegate; ISSM; ISSO; POA&M |
| SECURITY ASSESSMENT AND AUTHORIZATION | 37 | Is a current ATO and security authorization package available including, at a minimum: a signed version of the SSP, SAR, RAR, and POA&M? | JSIG CA-6 |  | ATO; security authorization package; signed version of the SSP; SAR; RAR; POA&M |
